final_candidates.decision_summary: The canonical naturally occurring OCT1 loss-of-function variant (literature R61C; arginine at position 60 in the given sequence) sits in a conserved substrate-recognition region and strongly reduces transport of most substrates while retaining measurable expression. Highest confidence for abolishing transport without gross destabilization.

Natural OCT1 variant (literature G401S; glycine at position 400 here) in a transmembrane segment with markedly reduced transport activity and relatively preserved protein abundance. A conservative glycine-to-serine change is unlikely to unfold the protein.

Proline-to-leucine in a transmembrane helix (position 340 here, literature P341L) disrupts the conformational cycling required for substrate translocation while likely preserving the folded helix bundle. Less direct support than the natural variants, hence lower confidence.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool is stable after position verification and self-review; further rounds without external evidence are unlikely to improve the Top-3.
